code.note: The shipped text contains the driver (DKCDY, DRIVER 6) and a printed run in the comments. Rerun must rebuild COLVI2 from the archive and run the test program; the claim is the PASS 1 global error line only.

claim.location: Shipped driver output, PASS 1 of the COLVI2 test run (decompressed archive text near line 9490: the COLVI2 SUMMARY block for DEFOPT=21, REQTOL=1e-3). The printed line is '-GLOB.ERR.EST.=  -.5782217549E-07    GLOB.ERR.=  -.1165398569E-06    SD =  6.93'. The claim is the GLOB.ERR. value (the actual global error at t=50 for the first component, as printed by the driver).
claim.metric: GLOB.ERR. of PASS 1 as printed by the driver (first component, t = 50)
claim.determinism: deterministic (the Volterra problem and the driver have no random input; the step size is fixed at 1.0 in this run)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 10 significant digits, so its rounding step is about 1e-16. The global error is about 1.2e-7 and is set by the method at REQTOL 1e-3, not by arithmetic roundoff; a rerun on IEEE arithmetic should move it far less than 1e-9 unless an iteration-count decision flips. The tolerance is 1% of the value. Not to be loosened after any run. The printed KEV, corrector-iteration and CP-second counts are NOT claimed: the count fields depend on convergence tests at roundoff, and CP seconds are machine-dependent.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the PASS 1 run is 50 steps of a 2-equation problem.
cost.data_size: None: the problem is fixed in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. The archive licence is not stated; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors' shipped driver prints a global error for a nonlinear Volterra solver on a fixed problem, a number that needs the full COLVI2 step and corrector loop to compute.
